messages.subject: Problem with MKL linking
parts:
On an archlinux system with intel-mkl and r-mkl installed from the AUR (respectively here and here), as soon as I try to run inla() in R, I get the following error:

.../R/library/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla: symbol lookup error: /opt/intel/mkl/lib/intel64/libmkl_gf_lp64.so: undefined symbol: mkl_serv_inspector_loaded
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully. If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>


I'm not really sure what I should do here... Any suggestions would be appreciated.

Thanks

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problem with MKL linking
parts:
Looks like there is a discrepancy in the MKL libs installed at your
system, and the ones used to compile. you can force to load the ones
in the R-INLA package, doing like I do here. By linking them to
'first', their in the ld-path that is in the first location and loaded
first. this should (I hope) solve your problem.

$ cd ~/R/x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu-
library/3.6/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/first/

hrue@localhost: ~/R/x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu-
library/3.6/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/first

$ ln -s ../lib*mkl* .

hrue@localhost: ~/R/x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu-
library/3.6/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/first

$ ls -l
total 0
-rw-r--r--. 1 hrue hrue 0 Oct 6 11:19 dummy
lrwxrwxrwx. 1 hrue hrue 17 Oct 10 15:00 libmkl_avx2.so ->
../libmkl_avx2.so

../libmkl_avx.so

../libmkl_core.so

../libmkl_def.so

../libmkl_sequential.so
